Rarity.rationale: Strawberry.cs:11 is RelicRarity.Common. EXECUTED (b15-pool): Common in the transcribed grab bag, obtainable from any relic reward.

HasUponPickupEffect.rationale: Matches Strawberry.cs:13 -- and it is the only one of this batch's four AfterObtained relics whose C# declares it, which is correct: the flag exists so RelicModel.IsTradable excludes a relic that has already spent its effect (relics/base.py:132-136 mirrors that), and Strawberry is the only Common (i.e. otherwise tradable) one of the four. relic/small_capsule, relic/storybook and relic/tanxs_whistle are all Ancient and untradable regardless, and none of their C# files declares the flag either.

AfterObtained.rationale: Strawberry.cs:17-20 is `CreatureCmd.GainMaxHp(Owner.Creature, DynamicVars.MaxHp.BaseValue)` and CreatureCmd.GainMaxHp (CreatureCmd.cs:786-799) raises max HP and then Heals by the same amount -- which run.gain_max_hp reproduces line for line, citing the same source. MaxHpVar(7m) (Strawberry.cs:15) has no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file, so 7 is the pinned non-ascension value and strawberry.py:16's MAX_HP = 7 is right. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b15.py b15-strawberry): a 40/80 player who takes Strawberry reaches 47/87. The relic's whole C# behaviour is faithful; the gap in this record is in the sim-only undo helper (guard G1).

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): `undo_after_obtained` (strawberry.py:21-25) CLAMPS instead of subtracting, so an un-granted Strawberry leaves up to 7 current HP behind -- contradicting its own comment
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the undo SUBTRACTS the heal instead of clamping. sts2_rl/relics/strawberry.py's after_obtained (MAX_HP 7) records the HP the grant actually healed in `_healed` and `undo_after_obtained` does `run.hp = max(1, run.hp - self._healed)` BEFORE `run.lose_max_hp(...)`, so the pair is exact from a damaged player as well as a full one. WAS: the undo called lose_max_hp and then re-clamped `run.hp = min(run.hp, run.max_hp)`, which gives back nothing whenever the post-heal HP is at or below the restored maximum -- the common case -- leaving the conformance runner's relic resync reading high for the rest of the run.

guards.what: N1: no per-combat or per-run state, no combat hooks at all
guards.rationale: Strawberry.cs has one override with an effect and no fields; strawberry.py adds nothing to __init__. PROMPT.md bug class 13 cannot apply, and `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py sweep-reset` puts it in neither the state buckets nor the frozen-constructor bucket -- confirmed here by reading both files in full rather than by trusting the sweep (PROMPT.md v6 item 1).

guards.what: N2: no IsAllowed / IsAllowedAtNeow override, and no ShowCounter / DisplayAmount
guards.rationale: PROMPT.md bug class 16's first half checked directly: Strawberry.cs (read in full) declares no IsAllowed override, so this relic is NOT in sweep B's 17-relic IsBeforeAct3TreasureChest cluster and the sim's missing `is_allowed` member costs nothing here. Its is_allowed_at_neow correctly stays at the base True (relics/base.py:159), matching RelicModel.IsAllowedAtNeow's default -- which, per PROMPT.md v6 item 2, DELEGATES to IsAllowed(runState) (RelicModel.cs:443-446), so with no IsAllowed override the two agree on both sides.
